Rashi on Shabbat 19a:10:1.english: And from their words we learned, etc. - And the practical difference [is] regarding the launderer's wage.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:11:2.english: How much do you want for it - As payment for laundering.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:11:3.english: The Sages already preceded you - For they taught us that white [garments] are more difficult to launder than dyed [garments].

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:11:4.english: He should measure it - He should measure it upon giving it and upon its return.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:11:5.english: Because he shrank it - In boiling [water].

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:1.hebrew: דאתי ממילא - כגון משקין הללו שנסחטים מאליהם, ובלבד שיתחיל מבעוד יום:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:1.english: That comes on its own - Such as these liquids that are squeezed out on their own, provided that he begins while it is still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:2.hebrew: בוסר - ענבים בתחילתן, כשהן דקים — מוציא מהן משקין לטבל בו בשר, לפי שהוא חזק וקרוב להחמיץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:2.english: Unripe grapes - Grapes at their beginning [of growth], when they are small — one extracts juice from them to dip meat into it, because it is strong and close to turning sour.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:3.hebrew: מלילות - שבולין שלא בשלו כל צרכן. מרסקן וטוענן באבנים, ומשקה זב מהן, ומטבל בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:3.english: Ears of grain - [These are] ears of grain that have not fully ripened. One crushes them and weighs them down with stones, and liquid flows from them, and one dips [food] into it.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:4.hebrew: יגמור - מאחר שרסקן וצברם בכובד, יניחם בכלים ויצאו מעצמן, ומותר לכתחילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:13:4.english: He may finish - Since he crushed them and piled them under a weight, he may leave them in the vessels and [the liquids] will come out on their own, and it is permitted ab initio.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:1:1.hebrew: כותח הבבלי - נותנין בו חמץ, כדאמרי' באלו עוברין. ואינו עשוי לאכול יחד, אלא לטבול בו, ואינו כלה עד זמן מרובה:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:1:1.english: Babylonian kutaḥ - Leaven is put into it, as we say in [the chapter entitled] Elu Ovrin. And it is not meant to be eaten all at once, but rather to dip into it; and it is not finished until a long time [has passed].

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:1:2.hebrew: שלשים יום - משמתחילין לדרוש בהלכות הפסח, חלה אזהרת פסח עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:1:2.english: Thirty days - From [the time] that they begin to expound the laws of Passover, the warning [regarding] Passover takes effect upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:2:1.english: A dog - It is incumbent upon him to feed it.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:4:1.hebrew: לא ישכיר אדם כליו - לעשות בהן מלאכה בע"ש, דנראה שמשכירו לו לצורך השבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:4:1.english: A person may not rent his utensils - [Even] to perform work with them on Shabbat eve, for it appears that he is renting them to him for the purpose of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:4:2.english: That his handwriting was not found - So that [the gentile] would not carry it on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:5:1.hebrew: אלא אם כן קצץ לו דמים - דכיון דקוצץ לו דמים, בדידיה טרח. וב"ש לא מודו בקצץ, דאפילו בקצץ פליגי, דהא לא עדיף ממוכר ומשאיל ונותן מתנה. אלא מילתא דב"ה אשמעינן, דבדלא קוצץ לא פליגי, דאסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:5:1.english: Unless he stipulated a set sum of money for him - For since he stipulates a set sum of money for him, [the gentile] is laboring for himself. And Beit Shammai do not concede when he fixed [a fee], for they disagree even when he fixed [a fee], as this is no better than [one who] sells, lends, or gives a gift. Rather, [the baraita] informs us of the position of Beit Hillel, [to teach] that where he does not fix [a fee], they do not disagree — that it is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:5:2.english: To his house - [The house] of the one to whom [the letter] was sent.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:5:3.english: To the house adjacent - To the wall of the city to which he was sent.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:6:1.hebrew: והלא קצץ - ואמאי אסרי ב"ה, הא אינהו שרו לעיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:6:1.english: Didn’t he stipulate a set [price] - And why do Beit Hillel prohibit [it], seeing that they themselves permitted [it] above?

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:7:1.hebrew: והא אמרת רישא אין משלחין - אא"כ קצץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:7:1.english: Didn’t you say in the first clause, “One may not send” - [That is,] unless he stipulated [a set price].

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:7:2.hebrew: דואר - שלטון העיר, ולו רגילין לשלוח איגרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:7:2.english: Doar - The ruler of the city, and to him [people] are accustomed to send letters.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:7:3.hebrew: שכיחא במתא - משלחין בלא קוצץ, בכדי שיגיע השליח: למר — לבית הדואר, ולמר — לבית הסמוך לחומה. ורישא, דאין משלחין בלא קוצץ כלל — דלא קביע במתא, ואם לא ימצאנו, יהא צריך לילך אחריו בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:7:3.english: [Where it is] frequently found in the city — one may send [a letter] without stipulating a price, provided there is sufficient time for the messenger to reach: according to one Master [representing Beit Hillel], the house of the mail carrier, and according to [the other] Master [representing Beit Hillel], the house adjacent to the wall. And the first clause [of the baraita, which states] that one may not send without stipulating a price at all, [is dealing with a case] where [the house of the mail carrier] is not permanently located in the city, and if [the messenger] does not find him, he will need to go after him on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:8:1.hebrew: מפליגין - מפרישין מן היבשה לים. וזהו לשון [הפלגת] ספינה — על שם שמפליג עצמו מן היישוב. ומרבינו יעקב שמעתי בעירובין, שאמצעיתו של ים נקרא פילגוס, ואף בלשון לעז — פילגס:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:8:1.english: Set sail - Departing from dry land to the sea. And this is the expression "[the setting sail of] a ship" — because one distances himself from the inhabited area. And from Rabbeinu Ya'akov I heard in [tractate] Eruvin that the middle of the sea is called pelagos, and in the vernacular [Old French] as well, pelegue.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:8:2.hebrew: ופוסק - עם הנכרי ע"מ לשבות, ואין צריך לשבות:
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:8:2.english: And he stipulates - With the gentile on the condition that he rest, and [the gentile] does not need to rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 19a:8:3.hebrew: ומצור לצידן - אין אלא מהלך יום, ובע"ש היה שם יום השוק, כדאמרינן בפסחים במקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נ:):
Rashi on Shabbat 19a:8:3.english: And from Tyre to Sidon - [It] is only a day's journey, and on Shabbat eve was the market day there, as we say in Pesachim in [the chapter entitled] Makom Shenahagu (Pesachim 50b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:13:1.hebrew: השום והבוסר והמלילות - למאי דקאמר בריש חבית (לקמן שבת קמג:): "מודים חכמים לר' יהודה בשאר פירות", ומייתי מדתניא: "סוחטין בפגעין ועוזרדין, אבל לא ברמונים" — צ"ל דשום ובוסר יותר עשוין למשקין מפגעין ועוזרדין. ומיהו התם מסיק, דתרדין, אע"ג דלאו בני סחיטה נינהו, הואיל ואחשבינהו — ה"ל משקין. ולפ"ז, הא דקתני "סוחטין בפגעים", לאו סחיטה גמורה קאמר, אלא מיתוק בעלמא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:13:1.english: "The garlic and the unripe grapes and the ears of grain" - According to what [the Gemara] says at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Ḥavit (below, Shabbat 143b): "The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Yehuda with regard to other fruits," and it cites from that which is taught [in a baraita]: "One may squeeze unripe figs and crab apples, but not pomegranates" — one must say that garlic and unripe grapes are more [commonly] designated for liquids than unripe figs and crab apples. However, there [the Gemara] concludes that with regard to beets, even though they are not [produce] subject to squeezing, since he ascribed importance to them, they are [considered] liquids. And according to this, that which [the baraita] taught, "One may squeeze unripe figs," does not mean actual squeezing, but merely sweetening [the fruit].

Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:13:2.hebrew: רבי ישמעאל אומר יגמור - פי': אינו צריך לסלק הטעינה סמוך לחשכה, אלא מניחן כל השבת. קשה לר"י: היכי מוכח דסבר ר' ישמעאל כל דאתי ממילא, אפי' עביד בשבת, ליכא חיוב חטאת? דילמא ר' ישמעאל סבר כב"ה, דשרו אפי' בהנך דלא אתי ממילא! והא דנקט "ריסקן" — משום רבותא דר"ע. ועוד תימה: דר"ע, דאמר "לא יגמור", לא כב"ש ולא כב"ה! ונראה לר"י: "דיגמור" — היינו דיגמור ויאכל בשבת; ולא דמי למשקין שזבו שאסורין, דגזרינן שמא יסחוט — דהכא, אפילו יסחוט, ליכא איסור דאורייתא, משום דאתי ממילא. והשתא מייתי שפיר: דקסבר ר' ישמעאל כל דאתי ממילא ש"ד, אפי' לב"ש, כיון דאי עביד ליה בשבת לא מיחייב. ור"ע דאמר "לא יגמור" — לא שצריך להסיר הקורה, דסבר כב"ה; אלא שלא יגמור כדי לאכול משקדש היום, דאסורין אפי' לב"ה כשאר משקין שזבו דאסורין, דהך סחיטה נמי דאורייתא, אע"ג דאתי ממילא. ועי"ל: דיגמור בידים משתחשך; דלא דמי למתני', דלא שרו ב"ה אלא טעינת קורה, אבל בידים לא; דהכא כשאין מחוסרין דיכה, כדאמר בסמוך. והשתא מייתי שפיר: דכיון דשרי ר' ישמעאל לסחוט בידים, ולא גזר אטו מחוסרי דיכה — א"כ במחוסרי דיכה נמי סבר דלא מיחייב. ובתר הכי קאמר: דלרבי ישמעאל במחוסרי דיכה מיחייב, ואפ"ה כשאין מחוסרין שרי בידים, ולא גזר אטו מחוסרין; אבל כר"ע לא אתיא, כיון דאסר בשאין מחוסרין דיכה אטו מחוסרין דיכה, מכלל דמחוסרין דיכה מיחייב, וא"כ אסור עם חשכה לב"ש:
Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:13:2.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: He may finish - [Rashi] explains: He does not need to remove the weight close to nightfall, but rather he leaves them [in place] the entire Shabbat. The Ri raised a difficulty: How is it proven [from this mishna] that Rabbi Yishmael holds that [with regard to] anything that comes on its own, even if one performs it on Shabbat, there is no liability for a sin-offering? Perhaps Rabbi Yishmael holds in accordance with Beit Hillel, who permit [leaving materials before Shabbat] even in those cases where it does not come on its own! And that which [the mishna] taught, "that he crushed them [while it was still day]," is to demonstrate the novelty of Rabbi Akiva's [stringency, that even though they were crushed by day, he forbids leaving them under the weight]. And furthermore, it is astonishing: for Rabbi Akiva, who says "he may not finish" [and must remove the weight], follows neither Beit Shammai nor Beit Hillel! And it appears to the Ri: "He may finish" means that he may finish [extracting the juice] and consume [it] on Shabbat. And it is not comparable to liquids that seeped out [from fruit on Shabbat], which are prohibited because we decree lest one squeeze [fruit directly] — for here, even if he were to squeeze [them], there is no Torah prohibition, because it comes on its own. And now [the Gemara] cites [this mishna as proof] well: for Rabbi Yishmael holds that anything that comes on its own is permitted even according to Beit Shammai, since if one were to perform it on Shabbat, he would not be liable [for a sin-offering]. And Rabbi Akiva, who says "he may not finish" — it is not that he must remove the beam, for he holds in accordance with Beit Hillel; rather, [it means] that he may not finish [extracting the juice] in order to consume [it] once the day has become sanctified, as [these liquids] are prohibited even according to Beit Hillel like other liquids that seeped out, which are prohibited because this squeezing is also [prohibited] by Torah law, even though it comes on its own. And one can further say: "He may finish" [means] by hand after it gets dark; for it is not comparable to our Mishnah, where Beit Hillel permitted only the loading of the beam [before Shabbat], but by hand, no; whereas here, it is when they do not lack pounding, as [the Gemara] states nearby. And now [the Gemara] cites [this mishna as proof] well: for since Rabbi Yishmael permits squeezing by hand and did not decree [a prohibition] due to [items that] lack pounding, if so, regarding [items that] lack pounding he also holds that one is not liable [for a sin-offering]. And subsequently, [the Gemara] says that according to Rabbi Yishmael, for [items that] lack pounding one is liable [for a sin-offering], and nevertheless when they do not lack [pounding] he permits [squeezing] by hand, and did not decree due to [items that] lack [pounding]; however, [our Mishnah] cannot follow Rabbi Akiva: since he prohibited [items that] do not lack pounding due to [items that] lack pounding, it implies that for [items that] lack pounding one is liable, and if so, it would be prohibited at nightfall according to Beit Shammai.

Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:3:1.hebrew: נותנין מזונות לנכרי בחצר - בשבת, אפילו לב"ש, דרגיל לאוכלו מיד. ודוקא מזונות, אבל שאר חפצים אסורים, אפילו לב"ה — דלא שרי ב"ה אלא בע"ש, אבל בשבת לא. וא"ת: ואמאי נותנין מזונות לנכרי בשבת? הא כיון דאין מזונותיהן עליך — כדאמרינן הכא, ובפ"ב דביצה (דף כא:) דמוציא אני את הנכרי שאין מזונותיהן עליך — ליתסר, כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא (דף קנה:) דאסור לטרוח בשבת לתת מזונות לפני חיה משום דאין מזונותי' עליך; ה"נ ה"ל למיסר בנכרי! ויש לומר: כיון דמפרנסים עניי נכרים עם עניי ישראל משום דרכי שלום, חשיב קצת מזונותיו עליך לענין איסור טורח שבות דרבנן; אבל לענין עשיית מלאכה בי"ט, דהוי איסור דאורייתא, לא חשיב מזונותיו עליך. כתוב בא"ז, שפ"א חלה נכרי, ושלח ליהודי א' בי"ט שישלח לו מיינו, ואם לא ישלח לו — ימות, והנכרי היה מוחזק בעיר; והתיר לשלוח לו ע"י נכרי משום דרכי שלום, ושלח אל רבינו שמחה והתיר לו, אבל לא ע"י ישראל. ולה"ר יצחק נראה, דהוא הדין בשבת: אם היה הענין כך, שהיה דבר ששייך דרכי שלום, כגון שהיה הנכרי אלם — נראה שמותר לשלוח לו על ידי נכרי, לדידן דלית לן השתא רשות הרבים דאורייתא [תוס' ישנים]:
Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:3:1.english: One may place food before the gentile in the courtyard - [This applies] on Shabbat, [and] even according to Beit Shammai, because he is accustomed to eating it immediately. And [it is] specifically food [that may be given], but other objects are forbidden [to be given to him], even according to Beit Hillel — for Beit Hillel only permitted [giving objects to a gentile] on Shabbat eve, but on Shabbat, no. And if you say: Why may one place food before a gentile on Shabbat? Behold, since responsibility for their sustenance is not incumbent upon you — as we say here, and in the second chapter of Beitzah (21b): "I exclude the gentile, for responsibility for their sustenance is not incumbent upon you" — let it be forbidden, just as we say in the last chapter [of Shabbat] (155b) that it is forbidden to exert effort on Shabbat to place food before a wild animal because responsibility for its sustenance is not incumbent upon you; so too, it should have been forbidden regarding a gentile! And one can say: Since we sustain the poor of gentiles along with the poor of the Jewish people for the sake of the ways of peace, his sustenance is considered somewhat incumbent upon you regarding the rabbinic decree prohibiting exertion; but regarding the performance of prohibited labor on Yom Tov, which is a Torah prohibition, his sustenance is not considered incumbent upon you. It is written in the Or Zarua that once a gentile fell ill and sent [word] to a certain Jew on Yom Tov to send him of his wine, and [warned] that if he did not send [it] to him, he would die; and the gentile was an influential person in the city. And he permitted sending [it] to him via a gentile for the sake of the ways of peace. And he sent [an inquiry] to Rabbeinu Simchah, and he permitted it to him, but not via a Jew. And to the Rabbi, Rabbi Yitzchak, it appeared that the same applies on Shabbat: if the matter was such that it was something to which [the consideration of] "the ways of peace" applies, for example if the gentile was a powerful and aggressive person, it appears that it is permitted to send to him via a gentile, according to our [circumstances], as nowadays we do not have a public domain by Torah law. [Tosafot Yeshanim]

Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:4:1.hebrew: לא ישכיר - אין לפרש משום שביתת כלים וכב"ש, דא"כ אפי' ברביעי ובחמישי נמי; אלא כב"ה היא, דלית להו שביתת כלים; או בחלוק וטלית וכיוצא בהן איירי, דלא שייך שביתת כלים. ואסור לפי שנראה כנוטל שכר שבת, אף על פי שמשכירו יחד חדש או שבוע — דאם משכירו ליום, אפילו ברביעי ובחמישי אסור, כדמשמע בסוף הזהב (ב"מ דף נח.) גבי שוכר פועלים לשמור פרה או תינוק. ודוקא לשוכרו, דמיחזי כנוטל שכר שבת; אבל שאלה שריא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:4:1.english: "A person may not rent" - One should not explain [that this prohibition is] due to the resting of utensils and according to Beit Shammai, for if so, even on Wednesday and Thursday [it should be forbidden] as well; rather, it is according to Beit Hillel, who do not hold of the resting of utensils; or, it is dealing with a tunic, a cloak, and the like, to which [the obligation of] the resting of utensils does not apply. And it is forbidden [on Shabbat eve] because it appears as though he is taking payment for Shabbat, even though he rents it out for a month or a week together — for if he rented it by the day, even on Wednesday and Thursday [it would be] forbidden, as is implied at the end of [the chapter] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 58a) regarding one who hires workers to guard a cow or a child. And [this prohibition applies] specifically to renting it out, since it appears as though he is taking payment for Shabbat; but lending is permitted.

Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:5:1.hebrew: אלא אם כן קוצץ לו דמים - מתני נמי דנותנים כלים לכובס ועורות לעבדן איירי נמי בקוצץ, והא דפריך "והלא קצץ" — לב"ה פריך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:5:1.english: "Unless he stipulates a set sum of money for him" - [Our] Mishnah as well, regarding giving garments to a launderer and hides to a tanner, also deals with [a case where one] stipulates a set price. And that which [the Gemara] challenges, "Did he not stipulate [a set price]?" — it challenges [the position of] Beit Hillel.

Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:8:1.hebrew: אין מפליגין בספינה - אפילו תוך התחום אסור משום שט, כדמוכח בפ' תולין (לקמן שבת קלט: ושם) גבי ההוא צורבא מדרבנן דאמר: "למינם בעינא", ואזיל לאידך גיסא ושמר פירי — משמע דתוך התחום היה, ואפ"ה בלא הערמה אסור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 19a:8:1.english: One may not set sail on a ship - Even within the [Shabbat] boundary, [traveling by boat] is forbidden due to [the decree against] swimming, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Tolin (below, Shabbat 139b, and there) regarding that young Torah scholar who said, "I want to sleep," and went to the other side and guarded fruit — which implies that it was within the [Shabbat] boundary, and even so, without artifice it was forbidden.
